title: Add JSON Schema structured output support (response_format, strict validation)
author: Jordan Lee
description: Motivation: provide first-class JSON Schema based structured-output support across the OpenAI-compat API surface so customers can declaratively request machine-parseable responses and get deterministic validation errors. This PR implements a response_format option that accepts "json_schema" with a schema payload and a mode flag (strict|lax). In strict mode responses that fail validation are rejected with a clear StructuredOutputValidationError and an optional debug_payload; in lax mode we attempt best-effort reconciliation and include a validation_warnings array in the response. The change covers server request parsing, streaming behavior (ensuring schema validation happens as tokens arrive when possible and falling back to full response validation when necessary), error shaping for the OpenAI-compat layer, SDK surface updates for Python/TS to expose the response_format helper, and docs + tests. Context: ties to ENG-4532 (structured output API spec) and ENG-4590 (compat layer streaming fixes). Checklist: - [x] server: parse response_format in request body and validate input schema size/complexity limits - [x] runtime: attach schema to generation pipeline and run incremental JSON well-formedness checks during streaming - [x] runtime: final schema validation pass using jsonschema and return structured error codes - [x] openai-compat: map errors to compatible error shape and update streaming protocol to include validation metadata events - [x] SDKs: convenience constructors and type hints (python/ts) - [x] docs: API docs + examples - [x] tests: unit + integration including strict/lax cases and streaming fragmentation edge cases Implementation notes: to avoid performance regressions we added a lightweight incremental parser that operates on the token stream and only invokes the full jsonschema validator at the end or when the incremental check indicates a structural violation. For small schemas we inline validation in the runtime path; for larger schemas we run validation on a worker thread to avoid blocking token emission. We included an escape hatch config server.feature.flags.structured_output_runtime to toggle new runtime behavior for canary rollout. Backwards compatibility: if response_format is omitted behavior unchanged. Error shape: StructuredOutputValidationError includes fields: code, message, validation_errors (list), and optional debug_payload (when debug enabled via header). OpenAI compat mapping: errors are surfaced as type APIError with code "invalid_response_format" when strict mode rejects, and as warnings in the usage metadata when lax mode used. Streaming: when streaming and strict mode is requested, the server will emit special STREAM_VALIDATION_EVENT tokens if it can determine an unrecoverable structural violation mid-stream; otherwise it buffers minimal state and validates at end. Tests: added streaming fragmentation tests that split objects across token boundaries and assert deterministic validation behavior. Rollout plan: merge to main and enable server flag for 10% canary; monitor structured_output.validation_failures metric and latency p95. Related PRs: SDK updates in repos redwood-sdk-python and redwood-sdk-typescript (follow-ups).
commits_summary: 3 commits: initial parser/runtime wiring; openai-compat error mapping and streaming event additions; docs/tests and SDK convenience helpers.
review_comments: Ava Chen: Please add a size/complexity limit for user-supplied schemas to avoid DoS; also include a unit test exercising a deeply nested schema.

Marcos Diaz: In streaming mode we should be careful not to increase tail latency. Can we run full validation off the hot path?
Jordan Lee (author): Full validation is offloaded to a worker thread for large schemas; incremental checks keep token emission in the hot path. Added notes in code and added a perf test.
Priya Kaur: Docs look good. Please add an example showing strict vs lax behavior and the exact OpenAI-compat error mapping.

release_notes: Added response_format=json_schema with strict and lax modes to OpenAI-compat API.
StructuredOutputValidationError returned for strict mode violations; lax mode returns validation_warnings.
SDK helpers (python/ts) for constructing json_schema requests and examples in docs.
